# Results {#sec-results}

Across the `r fmt(AREA_HA)` ha perimeter and the `r spellnum(nrow(ARS))` outbreak years from `r min(ARS$year)` to `r max(ARS$year)`, attack was clustered in every year, with `r num(min(ASPT$joins_bb / ASPT$joins_bb_null), "%.1f")` to `r num(max(ASPT$joins_bb / ASPT$joins_bb_null), "%.1f")` times as many neighbouring pairs of attacked cells as random permutation produced and positive autocorrelation to a median of `r fmt(median(ASPT$range_m))` m (Figure S17). Attack in the cell and within `r A_NB` m the year before dominated every model it entered. A cell attacked the year before had `r num(exp(acv("lagyr_self", dep = TRUE)), "%.1f")` times the odds of attack, and the two terms raised the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of M3 from `r num(aft("M3", FALSE, "auc", "with previous year"))` to `r num(aft("M3", TRUE, "auc"))`. Of the `r nrow(SCRT)` candidate variables, `r sum(SCRT$lr_p < 0.05)` improved the fit by likelihood ratio test once the dependence terms were in the model, the elastic net kept `r sum(SCRT$enet != 0)`, and the largest variance inflation among the main effects of M3 was `r num(max(SCRT$vif[SCRT$in_m3]), "%.1f")` (@tbl-variables; Table S13). Each estimate below is a change in log-odds per standard deviation with the dependence terms in the model unless stated otherwise.

## Refugia mechanisms

The first question asked whether stand density, shading by terrain and the scarcity of large trees predicted attack once attack nearby was in the model. The refugia hypothesis predicted less attack in thin stands, on ground shaded by terrain and in stands without large trees. Density and shade moved as predicted and host size did not. Attack rose with stand basal area, `r ac("BASAL_AREA", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("BASAL_AREA", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`), so the thinnest stands had the least attack. The term was `r ac("BASAL_AREA")` without the dependence terms (`r ac("BASAL_AREA", col = "p")`), `r afl("BASAL_AREA")` under the spatial field (`r afl("BASAL_AREA", "p")`) and `r agr("BASAL_AREA", 270)` at a 270 m grain (`r agr("BASAL_AREA", 270, "p")`), and basal area lowered AIC by `r fmt(aft("M0") - aft("M1"))` when it entered, more than any other step of the sequence (@tbl-final; @fig-coefficients; Table S9). Crown closure gave the same direction in the sixteen-day model, `r wc("E2", "CROWN_CLOSURE")` (`r wc("E2", "CROWN_CLOSURE", "p")`), while live stems per hectare, which counted small trees as well as large, ran the other way, `r wc("E2", "VRI_LIVE_STEMS_PER_HA")` (`r wc("E2", "VRI_LIVE_STEMS_PER_HA", "p")`). The sun of the flight window raised attack in dense stands and not in thin ones, by `r asl("BASAL_AREA:solar_flight_direct", "solar_flight_direct", 1, TRUE)` (`r asl("BASAL_AREA:solar_flight_direct", "solar_flight_direct", 1, TRUE, "p")`) one standard deviation above the mean basal area against `r asl("BASAL_AREA:solar_flight_direct", "solar_flight_direct", -1, TRUE)` (`r asl("BASAL_AREA:solar_flight_direct", "solar_flight_direct", -1, TRUE, "p")`) one below it.

Ground shaded by terrain had less attack. Sky view, the share of the sky a cell saw, entered at `r ac("sky_view", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("sky_view", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`) and the direct sun of the flight window at `r ac("solar_flight_direct", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("solar_flight_direct", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`), so attack rose with open sky and with sun, as the hypothesis predicted. Northness ran against it. Ground facing north had more attack, `r ac("northness", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("northness", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`), and the term grew under the spatial field to `r afl("northness")` (`r afl("northness", "p")`), while sky view fell under the field to `r afl("sky_view")` (`r afl("sky_view", "p")`) and was `r agr("sky_view", 270)` at a 270 m grain (`r agr("sky_view", 270, "p")`). Shade by terrain therefore protected ground at 30 m once attack nearby was in the model, and the protection did not survive the field, whereas the warmth of a south face protected nothing at any grain.

The hypothesis predicted less attack where large trees were few, so attack rising with tree size. Attack instead fell with quadratic mean diameter, `r ac("QUAD_DIAM_125", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("QUAD_DIAM_125", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`), and `r afl("QUAD_DIAM_125")` under the field (`r afl("QUAD_DIAM_125", "p")`). By diameter class, attack rose from `r dia("20-25")` per cent of the balanced sample at 20 to 25 cm to `r dia("25-30")` per cent at 25 to 30 cm and fell to `r dia("30-40")` per cent at 30 to 40 cm and `r dia(">40")` per cent above 40 cm \[χ²(`r ADIT$df`) = `r num(ADIT$chisq, "%.1f")`, `r pthr(ADIT$p)`, Cramér's V = `r num(ADIT$cramers_v)`\], a step of `r num(ADIT$step_diff, "%.1f")` percentage points across the 25 cm source threshold (95 per cent confidence interval `r num(ADIT$step_ci_lo, "%.1f")` to `r num(ADIT$step_ci_hi, "%.1f")`, `r pthr(ADIT$step_p)`). The stands of the largest trees held the least pine, `r num(ADIA$pine_ba[ADIA$bin == ">40"], "%.1f")` m² ha⁻¹ of susceptible pine basal area against `r num(ADIA$pine_ba[ADIA$bin == "25-30"], "%.1f")` at 25 to 30 cm, and susceptible pine basal area itself entered at `r ac("PINE_BA", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("PINE_BA", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`). Host size therefore acted as a threshold at 25 cm and not as the gradient the hypothesis described. Elevation had the largest coefficient of any environmental term, `r ac("elevation", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("elevation", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`).

## Wind and openness

The second question asked whether wind during flight lowered attack more in open stands than in closed ones, as disruption of the pheromone plume predicted, so that the wind term should be negative in open stands and weaker or positive in closed ones. It was, with the terrain wind of the previous summer in the sixteen-day model. The speed itself was `r wc("E2 modelled wind", "wnlag_speed")` at the mean crown closure (`r wc("E2 modelled wind", "wnlag_speed", "p")`), its interaction with crown closure was `r wc("E2 modelled wind", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed")` (`r wc("E2 modelled wind", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed", "p")`), and the wind effect was `r wss("E2 modelled wind", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed", "wnlag_speed", -1)` (`r wss("E2 modelled wind", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed", "wnlag_speed", -1, "p")`) in stands one standard deviation below the mean crown closure and `r wss("E2 modelled wind", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed", "wnlag_speed", 1)` (`r wss("E2 modelled wind", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed", "wnlag_speed", 1, "p")`) one above it (Figure S16; Table S4). The wind at 10 m gave the same pattern, an interaction of `r wc("E2 modelled wind, 10 m", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed10")` (`r wc("E2 modelled wind, 10 m", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed10", "p")`) with a wind effect of `r wss("E2 modelled wind, 10 m", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed10", "wnlag_speed10", -1)` (`r wss("E2 modelled wind, 10 m", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed10", "wnlag_speed10", -1, "p")`) in open stands and `r wss("E2 modelled wind, 10 m", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed10", "wnlag_speed10", 1)` (`r wss("E2 modelled wind, 10 m", "CROWN_CLOSURE:wnlag_speed10", "wnlag_speed10", 1, "p")`) in closed ones. Wind also lowered attack in stands of small trees and not in stands of large ones, `r wss("E2 modelled wind", "QUAD_DIAM_125:wnlag_speed", "wnlag_speed", -1)` (`r wss("E2 modelled wind", "QUAD_DIAM_125:wnlag_speed", "wnlag_speed", -1, "p")`) one standard deviation below the mean diameter against `r wss("E2 modelled wind", "QUAD_DIAM_125:wnlag_speed", "wnlag_speed", 1)` (`r wss("E2 modelled wind", "QUAD_DIAM_125:wnlag_speed", "wnlag_speed", 1, "p")`) above it.

The station wind interpolated from the valleys did not show the effect. The wind of the same period raised attack, `r wc("E2", "ep_wind_flight")` (`r wc("E2", "ep_wind_flight", "p")`), as did the previous summer's, `r wc("E2 lagged, diameter and closure", "ep_windlag_flight")` (`r wc("E2 lagged, diameter and closure", "ep_windlag_flight", "p")`), and its interaction with crown closure could not be distinguished from zero (`r wc("E2 lagged, diameter and closure", "CROWN_CLOSURE:ep_windlag_flight", "p")`). In the annual models the July station wind raised attack, `r ac("jul", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("jul", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`), by `r asl("BASAL_AREA:jul", "jul", -1, TRUE)` (`r asl("BASAL_AREA:jul", "jul", -1, TRUE, "p")`) in stands one standard deviation below the mean basal area and `r asl("BASAL_AREA:jul", "jul", 1, TRUE)` (`r asl("BASAL_AREA:jul", "jul", 1, TRUE, "p")`) one above it, the same order as the sixteen-day result but with no fall in attack at any density.

## Shelter and deposition

The third question asked whether ground sheltered from the afternoon wind, or facing away from it, had more attack whatever the stand, as deposition predicted. The wind shelter index was higher on slopes facing the prevailing wind, so the prediction was a negative coefficient and no interaction with basal area. Both held, and the first was weak. The index entered at `r ac("wind_shelter", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("wind_shelter", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`), from `r ac("wind_shelter")` without the dependence terms (`r ac("wind_shelter", col = "p")`), and its interaction with basal area could not be distinguished from zero (`r ac("BASAL_AREA:wind_shelter", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`), so the effect did not depend on the stand. It was `r agr("wind_shelter", 90)` at a 90 m grain (`r agr("wind_shelter", 90, "p")`) and changed sign under the spatial field, to `r afl("wind_shelter")` (`r afl("wind_shelter", "p")`), with residual Moran's I still at a median of `r num(median(ASMO$moran_i[ASMO$model == "with spatial field"]))` under the field.

The terrain wind gave the same direction more strongly. The shelter index at each cell's own modelled wind direction entered at `r ac("wnlag_shelter", "M3 shelter at the modelled wind", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("wnlag_shelter", "M3 shelter at the modelled wind", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`) in the annual model and `r wc("E2 shelter at the modelled wind", "wnlag_shelter")` (`r wc("E2 shelter at the modelled wind", "wnlag_shelter", "p")`) in the sixteen-day model, the share of flight hours in which the wind blew upslope at `r wc("E2 upslope share", "wnlag_upslope")` (`r wc("E2 upslope share", "wnlag_upslope", "p")`) over sixteen days and `r ac("wnlag_upslope", "M3 upslope share", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("wnlag_upslope", "M3 upslope share", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`) annually, and the slope updraft, the wind pushed up the face, at `r wc("E2 slope updraft", "wnlag_oro")` (`r wc("E2 slope updraft", "wnlag_oro", "p")`) over sixteen days and `r ac("wnlag_oro", "M3 slope updraft", dep = TRUE)` (`r ac("wnlag_oro", "M3 slope updraft", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`) annually, falling most steeply on ridges and spurs, `r wc("E2 slope updraft at ridges", "tpi:wnlag_oro")` (`r wc("E2 slope updraft at ridges", "tpi:wnlag_oro", "p")`). The faces that met the south-west afternoon wind had the least attack, `r fpa("south")` per cent of cells facing south and `r fpa("south-west")` per cent facing south-west against `r fpa("west")` per cent facing west and `r fpa("north-west")` per cent facing north-west (@fig-flight-paths). Ridges and valleys had less attack than slopes without the dependence terms, `r ac("geomorphonridge")` (`r ac("geomorphonridge", col = "p")`) and `r ac("geomorphonvalley")` (`r ac("geomorphonvalley", col = "p")`), and neither differed from slopes once attack nearby was in the model (`r ac("geomorphonridge", dep = TRUE, col = "p")` and `r ac("geomorphonvalley", dep = TRUE, col = "p")`; @tbl-final).

The remaining terms, surface temperature, the lidar terrain, convective lift, the back-trajectories, pressure, valley and ridge flatness, cold-air pooling, canopy height, winter cold, the upwind sources and the maps of 2012, were fitted beside M3 and E2 and none entered the final models (Tables S11 and S12).
